what_its_for: Doxycycline is an antibiotic used to treat many types of bacterial infections. These include chest infections, skin infections, sexually transmitted infections (such as chlamydia), Lyme disease, urinary tract infections, eye infections, and certain tick-borne illnesses. It is also used to treat or prevent malaria, and to help with severe acne.
how_to_take: Take doxycycline exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the tablet or capsule whole with a full glass of water (at least 8 ounces). Do NOT crush, break, or chew delayed-release tablets. You may take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach, but avoid taking it with dairy products alone or antacids right away, as these can make the medicine less effective. Stay upright — do not lie down for at least 30 minutes after taking it to avoid irritating your throat or esophagus. Always finish the full course of antibiotics, even if you feel better early.
dosing: Your dose depends on the condition being treated. A common adult dose is 100 mg taken twice a day (every 12 hours), or sometimes 200 mg once a day. For acne or malaria prevention, the dose may be different. Your doctor will tell you exactly how much to take and for how long. Do not take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this can increase your risk of side effects.
storage: Store doxycycline at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use doxycycline past its expiration date — expired doxycycline can actually be harmful to your kidneys. Dispose of unused medicine properly through a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid lying down for at least 30 minutes after taking your dose. Avoid taking doxycycline with milk, dairy products, antacids containing calcium, magnesium, or aluminum, iron supplements, or vitamins containing minerals within 2 hours of your dose, as they can block the medicine from working. Avoid too much sun exposure — doxycycline makes your skin much more sensitive to sunlight and can cause severe sunburns. Use sunscreen, wear protective clothing, and avoid tanning beds. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Do not take with other antibiotics unless specifically directed by your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe skin rash, hives, or blistering; difficulty breathing or swallowing; swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; severe stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhea (especially if it contains blood or mucus); yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); severe headache or blurred vision; pain or difficulty swallowing; signs of a new infection (fever, chills, unusual discharge). Also let your doctor know if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting doxycycline, but it is important to keep taking all of your doses even if you feel well. For infections, most people notice improvement within 2 to 3 days. For acne, it may take 6 to 12 weeks to see a noticeable improvement. For malaria prevention, start taking it 1 to 2 days before travel and continue for 4 weeks after returning.
special_populations: Children: Doxycycline is generally NOT recommended for children under 8 years old because it can permanently stain developing teeth and affect bone growth. It may be used in younger children only for serious infections like anthrax or certain tick-borne illnesses when no alternatives are available. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Doxycycline should NOT be used during pregnancy (especially in the second and third trimesters) or while breastfeeding, as it can harm the baby's developing teeth and bones. Talk to your doctor about safer antibiotic options if you are pregnant or nursing. Kidney or Liver Problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or a different antibiotic may be recommended. Older Adults: Older adults can generally take doxycycline safely, but should take extra precautions to avoid sun exposure and to take the medicine with plenty of water to protect the esophagus.
